description: This is the first annual overview of major ICT-related incidents in the EU financial sector reported under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), covering incidents in 2025. It gives, on an anonymised and aggregated basis, the number of major incidents by month and sector, the criteria that triggered reporting, domestic or cross-border impact, incident types, threats and techniques for cyber incidents, root causes, the share originating from ICT third-party service providers, and effects on transactions and financial counterparties. It is produced by the Joint Committee of the European Supervisory Authorities, EBA, EIOPA and ESMA, as required by Article 22 of DORA, and was published on 3 June 2026. Coverage is the EU: 3,383 major incidents were reported, 0.18 per entity subject to DORA, mostly in the credit and payments sectors; about one third had cross-border impact, system failures and external events were the main drivers, and only 10% related to cybersecurity. The report is a free PDF. Caveats: data are aggregated charts, not an incident list, differences between sectors partly reflect reporting practice, and the pages give no reuse licence. For simulation it supplies base rates and cause distributions for outage and cyber scenarios in resilience and cascading failure models of financial infrastructure. It is related to the TARGET2 outage case study record in this catalogue, a detailed single incident.
